title: Degree-zero Koszul boundaries are saturated under a quotient-regular scalar
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module, r>=0, f : Fin r -> R and t in R. Let A=K(f) tensor_R M [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] and assume multiplication by t is injective on M/(Ideal.ofList (List.ofFn f))*M, in the IsSMulRegular sense used in [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. If b in A_0 and t*b=d_A a for some a in A_1, then b=d_A c for some c in A_1. No positive-degree acyclicity or regularity of f is assumed.

source.place: Tag 062F, degree-zero quotient calculation, and Tag 0623, the degree-one Koszul differential; step 1 and the degree-one part of step 3 of the regular-sequence node; read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/062F and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0629 because the literature source is not present on this machine

proof.text: Identify the degree-zero exterior power with R and the degree-one exterior power with Fin r ->0 R using exteriorPower.zeroEquiv and oneEquiv [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis]. On the canonical degree-one alternating generators, contractLeft_ι identifies the differential with Finsupp.linearCombination R f. Exterior-power extensionality gives this formula on the entire first term. Tensor it with M and use TensorProduct.lid: the boundary of x tensor m maps to linearCombination(f)(oneEquiv(x))*m.

Under the resulting zero-term equivalence e, prove range(e composed with d_A)=Ideal.ofList(List.ofFn f)*top. For the inclusion into the ideal multiple, induct on tensors and use Finsupp.range_linearCombination. Conversely every scalar in the generated ideal is linearCombination(f)(x) for a finitely supported x, and its multiple of m is the boundary of oneEquiv.symm(x) tensor m. Submodule.smul_le combines these preimages to give the reverse inclusion.

The assumption t*b=d_A a places t*e(b) in this ideal multiple. Apply injectivity of multiplication by t to the quotient class of e(b) to show that class is zero. Quotient.mk_eq_zero puts e(b) in the computed boundary range. Extract a preimage c and use the injectivity of e to conclude d_A c=b. The proof also applies when r=0 or M is the zero module.
